chapter_theme: A song at Kadambur (கடம்பூர்): the poet describes dancing women who invite a man in, demand money and leave in spite when it is not enough, and asks not to go where they are; the praise names Vishnu as uncle and Siva's dance sung by Narada and Tumburu.

757.reading: The poet describes dancing women who say 'come here, this is the house', tell their maids to spread the mat, speak like courteous hosts and take a man to bed, then before joining him say the cash and the cloth are not enough and go off in spite; he asks not to go where they are and to be given Murugan's cool feet. The praise names Narayana, Rama, Kesava with the discus as his uncle, Siva who dances while Narada and Tumburu sing as his father, and the vel that sent Sura's sea to ruin so the sun's chariot could run, at Kadambur where the Kaveri and Seeraru meet.
757.nuance: The women's own speech is quoted (வாரும் இங்கே வீடிதோ, வாடி பெண்காள் பாயைப் போடும்), as in Kural and Naladiyar warnings; ஆசார வாசகம் போல், like words of courtesy, names the pretence. காசு ஆடை போதாமை is the turn: love lasts until the price falls short. Some words of the opening (பணம் பாஷாணம், மால் கடந்தே போம் மேனி) are hard to construe.

links.note: The Naladiyar says the harlot's love ends when the hand is empty, like a lamp without oil; 757 shows the moment, the woman leaving the bed because the cash and cloth are not enough.
